Alright, let me think through this year like I do every spring sitting with my tea.

**My land and my situation**

I got 14 mu total. Been farming this ground for 50 years, my father farmed it before me. Two of my kids work in town now — they come back for the busy times but I can't count on them for daily work. My wife still helps, she's 68. The grandkids are in school.

I split my land like always: 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation on the better flat ground near the well, and 4 mu in cotton on the sandier piece to the west. Cotton takes too much hand work for my back now, so I don't want more than that. But cotton cash is good when the price holds, and I've grown it my whole life.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October)**

My wheat is heading out now. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 jin per mu (that's 20 kg), and I topdressed with urea at jointing in March — maybe one bag per 3 mu, however it came out. Neighbors did similar. I irrigated once before winter, once at jointing. Wheat looks okay this year, not as yellow as two years ago when I was short on fertilizer money. If the rain comes I might skip the next irrigation, pumping costs too much now. Expecting around 400 kg per mu, same as usual.

**Maize (goes in after wheat harvest in June)**

Right after wheat harvest I hire the man in the next village with the no-till planter — costs me about 25 yuan per mu but saves me three days. I can't plow by hand anymore. I use hybrid seed from the shop, the one the neighbor Old Wang bought last year that did well for him. Fertilizer goes in with the planter, maybe 30 jin compound per mu, and I topdress urea when it's knee-high if the price is reasonable. One irrigation at tasseling if July is dry. Expect about 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton (planting now, late April)**

I'll plant cotton next week when the soil warms up enough. I buy seed from the cooperative — can't save it, they're hybrids. Cotton needs less nitrogen than grain but some potash, I put down compound at planting, about 30 jin per mu. Picking is the hard part — my wife and I do first pick, then I pay the women from the village for second and third pick, 80 yuan a day. I spray for bollworm when I see it, not before. Expect maybe 250 kg lint per mu, depends on the weather in August.

**What I'm watching this year**

Urea went up again. I might stretch my topdress a little thinner on the maize if the price doesn't come down. If we get a dry May my cotton will need more watering than I'd like. Main thing is I don't want any big surprises — I keep some cash aside in case the pump breaks.
